extracted.intended_audience: general public, journalists, and PR/communications professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Investigative news story documenting alleged unethical and deceptive practices by a public relations firm (Bell Pottinger) and the industry/regulatory findings about those practices. Focuses on campaigns, social media manipulation, covert operations, and professional-ethical breaches in PR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid inciting racial hatred / inflaming racial discord
rubrics_metrics.description: PRCA investigation found the company had launched a campaign which was "likely to inflame racial discord in South Africa" and that Bell Pottinger’s work had “incited racial hatred”.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not create messaging that divides communities on racial lines or frames political opponents as racial enemies (example: labelling opponents as “white monopoly capital”). Materials that amplify racial tensions are considered unethical and may lead to regulatory sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not bring the PR and communications industry into disrepute
rubrics_metrics.description: PRCA: Bell Pottinger’s actions “brought the PR and communications industry into disrepute”.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid practices that damage public trust in the industry (covert manipulation, deceptive campaigns, racially divisive content). Regulators may expel firms whose conduct undermines the profession's reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to relevant ethical principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Herbert Smith Freehills found some material was “potentially racially divisive… and was created in breach of relevant ethical principles”.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure campaigns comply with professional ethical standards (avoid discrimination, hate-inciting content, and other breaches). Commission independent ethical reviews where campaigns touch on sensitive social issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use deceptive social amplification (bots/astroturfing)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bureau identified dozens of Twitter accounts used to amplify the message; analysis indicates these accounts are "bots" - fake accounts set up to resemble real Twitter users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid creating or using fake social accounts or purchasing networks of retweets to simulate grassroots support. Such astroturfing is an anti-pattern; while services are readily available and hard to trace, their use risks reputational and regulatory consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not run covert propaganda disguised as local/independent media
rubrics_metrics.description: Bureau revealed a secret $500 million propaganda operation in Iraq that involved making videos which would look like they had been produced by local Iraqi TV stations to spin the news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not produce content that intentionally misrepresents its source (e.g., fake local TV, fabricated independent outlets). Transparency about origin and sponsorship is required; covert operations that deceive audiences are unethical and potentially subject to legal/regulatory action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid manipulative 'dark arts' tactics (SEO, political influence, attacks on journalists)
rubrics_metrics.description: PR agents boasted of their ability to use "dark arts" to influence public opinion, manipulate Google results to "drown out" negative coverage, and use MPs to attack journalists over minor reporting errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not employ covert SEO manipulation to bury negative content, use political contacts to intimidate critics, or orchestrate attacks on journalists. Such tactics are ethically questionable and damage both client and industry reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not covertly edit or manipulate public information sources (e.g., Wikipedia)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bell Pottinger claimed it had a team dealing with negative Wikipedia coverage; evidence included removal of references and editing of material related to clients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid undisclosed or deceptive editing of encyclopedias and other public information resources intended to conceal adverse facts. If managing online profiles, ensure transparency, proper disclosure, and conformity with platform policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose funding, clients and conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: The article highlights secret payments (eg. $500 million from the Pentagon) and difficulties identifying who paid for social amplification; covert funding was central to criticisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain clear disclosure of clients, funding sources, and material conflicts of interest. Secret or undeclared payments for influence operations or paid amplification increase risk of ethical breaches and public backlash.
